concerns.text: Task T000 mandates executing the baseline in a 'high-fidelity simulated environment' and labeling output as 'Sim-Baseline'. This violates FR-004 and SC-001 which require the baseline to be the 'original RoboDojo Neural Policy' executed in the 'real-world environment' to validly test the sim-to-real gap. The task silently relaxes the requirement for real-world ground truth by authorizing simulation as a substitute.

The contingency clause in T000 ('If the real-world robot is unavailable... log as Sim-Baseline') violates Constitution Principle III (Data Hygiene) and the Plan's explicit constraint: 'Real-world execution data is the ground truth (no synthetic data generation for final metrics)'. This task introduces a fallback to synthetic/simulated data for the primary baseline comparison, weakening the research validity.

Task T010 describes training a 'Linear Probe' on a split of the 'RoboDojo dataset' without explicitly mandating the use of the 'real-world videos' required by FR-009 ('using a set of real-world videos to adapt the low-level controller for domain shift'). This risks training on simulation data, failing to address the domain shift, and violating the specific data source requirement of the FR.

Task T036 explicitly excludes 'Hardware Error' and 'Timeout' from the 'catastrophic failure' calculation. SC-005 defines catastrophic failures as 'complete task abandonment due to unmodeled dynamics'. In a real-world context, hardware stalls and timeouts are primary manifestations of unmodeled dynamics. Excluding them artificially lowers the failure rate, violating the intent and measurement definition of SC-005.

Task T037 defines the Oracle Executor using the 'MuJoCo physics engine'. While the Plan notes this is 'diagnostic only', Constitution Principle VI (Simulation Fidelity Independence) mandates that metrics be derived from 'real-world' execution to test topological sufficiency. Using a high-fidelity physics simulator (MuJoCo) for the control experiment reintroduces the continuous physics variables the project seeks to isolate, contradicting the principle's core constraint.

Task T022 instructs to 'raise ResourceLimitExceeded error and abort' if RAM > 6 GB. SC-003 and US-1 Acceptance Scenario 3 state the process 'MUST NOT crash due to OOM errors' and implies the system must remain stable to process the tasks. A hard abort prevents the collection of partial data and violates the stability requirement, potentially blocking the statistical analysis (US-3) entirely if a single task exceeds the limit.
